L11: # The Direction of Updatable Encryption Does Matter
L12:

L35: ## Abstract
L36: We introduce a new definition for key updates, called backward-leak uni-directional key updates, in updatable encryption (UE). This notion is a variant of uni-directional key updates for UE. We show that existing secure UE schemes in the bi-directional key updates setting are not secure in the backward-leak uni-directional key updates setting. Thus, security in the backward-leak uni-directional key updates setting is strictly stronger than security in the bi-directional key updates setting.
L37: This result is in sharp contrast to the equivalence theorem by Jiang (Asiacrypt 2020), which says security in the bi-directional key updates setting is equivalent to security in the existing uni-directional key updates setting. We call the existing uni-directional key updates “forward-leak uni-directional” key updates to distinguish two types of uni-directional key updates in this paper.
L38: We also present two UE schemes with the following features.
L39: 
L40:   * The first scheme is post-quantum secure in the backward-leak uni-directional key updates setting under the learning with errors assumption.
L41: 
L42:   * The second scheme is secure in the no-directional key updates setting and based on indistinguishability obfuscation and one-way functions. This result solves the open problem left by Jiang (Asiacrypt 2020).
L43:

L106: ### 【20†Unidirectional Updatable Encryption and Proxy Re-encryption from DDH】
L107: 
L108: Chapter © 2023
L109: ## Notes
L110: 
L111:   1. 1.
L112: 
L113: The other variant is ciphertext-dependent updates UE, where we need not only two secret keys but also a part of ciphertext (called header) to generate a token [【21†BLMR13】, 【22†EPRS17】, 【23†BEKS20】]. Ciphertext-independent updates UE is more efficient.
L114: 
L115:   2. 2.
L116: 
L117: Note that Jain, Lin,and Sahai achieve IO from well-founded assumptions, the SXDH, LWE, a variant of LPN, and PRG in \(\mathsf {NC}^0\) [【24†JLS21】]. See their paper for the detail of the assumptions.
L118: 
L119:   3. 3.
L120: Their paper [【25†SS21】] appeared on Cryptology ePrint archive right after the initial version of this paper (【26†https://eprint.iacr.org/2021/221/20210311:210911†eprint.iacr.org】) appeared on Cryptology ePrint archive. The comparison here is based on the latest versions of their and our papers.
L121: 
L122:   4. 4.
L123: Everspaugh et al. [【22†EPRS17】] presented a ciphertext-independent UE scheme from authenticated encryption (AE). However, they assume an AE scheme is secure against related key attacks. So far, it seems that we need the power of public key encryption (such as DDH) to achieve related key secure AE [【27†HLL16】]. In addition, Everspaugh et al. retracted the ciphertext-independent construction in their full version paper (【28†https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/527/20180903:192110†eprint.iacr.org】).
